content.overview: BNS s. 30 — Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent. BNS restatement of IPC 92. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 92. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 30 is the rule on “Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent”. The section provides that nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person’s consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent, or if that person is incapable of giving consent, and has no guardian or other person in lawful charge of him from whom it is possible to obtain consent in time for the thing to be done with benefit:. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 30 exists so that “Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent” has a closed legal test in Chapter III — General Exceptions. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: When an act is not an offence: mistake, accident, infancy, unsoundness, consent, compulsion — and the right of private defence.

The provision in detail
30. Nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person’s consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent, or if that person is incapable of giving consent, and has no guardian or other person in lawful charge of him from whom it is possible to obtain consent in time for the thing to be done with benefit:

(a) the intentional causing of death, or the attempting to cause death;

(b) the doing of anything which the person doing it knows to be likely to cause death, for any purpose other than the preventing of death or grievous hurt, or the curing of any grievous disease or infirmity;

(c) the voluntary causing of hurt, or to the attempting to cause hurt, for any purpose other than the preventing of death or hurt;

(d) the abetment of any offence, to the committing of which offence it would not extend

(1) Z is thrown from his horse, and is insensible. A, a surgeon, finds that Z requires to be trepanned. A, not intending Z’s death, but in good faith, for Z’s benefit, performs the trepan before Z recovers his power of judging for himself. A has committed no offence

(2) Z is carried off by a tiger. A fires at the tiger knowing it to be likely that the shot may kill Z, but not intending to kill Z, and in good faith intending Z’s benefit. A’s bullet gives Z a mortal wound. A has committed no offence

(3) A, a surgeon, sees a child suffer an accident which is likely to prove fatal unless an operation be immediately performed. There is no time to apply to the child’s guardian. A performs the operation in spite of the entreaties of the child, intending, in good faith, the child’s benefit. A has committed no offence

(4) A is in a house which is on fire, with Z, a child. People below hold out a blanket. A drops the child from the house top, knowing it to be likely that the fall may kill the child, but not intending to kill the child, and intending, in good faith, the child’s benefit. Here, even if the child is killed by the fall, A has committed no offence

Essential ingredients
1. Nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person’s consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent, or if that person is incapable of giving consent, and has no guardian or other person in lawful charge of him from whom it is possible to obtain consent in time for the thing to be done with benefit:
2. (a) the intentional causing of death, or the attempting to cause death;
3. (b) the doing of anything which the person doing it knows to be likely to cause death, for any purpose other than the preventing of death or grievous hurt, or the curing of any grievous disease or infirmity;
4. (c) the voluntary causing of hurt, or to the attempting to cause hurt, for any purpose other than the preventing of death or hurt;
5. (d) the abetment of any offence, to the committing of which offence it would not extend
6. (1) Z is thrown from his horse, and is insensible. A, a surgeon, finds that Z requires to be trepanned. A, not intending Z’s death, but in good faith, for Z’s benefit, performs the trepan before Z recovers his power of judging for himself. A has committed no offence
7. (2) Z is carried off by a tiger. A fires at the tiger knowing it to be likely that the shot may kill Z, but not intending to kill Z, and in good faith intending Z’s benefit. A’s bullet gives Z a mortal wound. A has committed no offence
8. (3) A, a surgeon, sees a child suffer an accident which is likely to prove fatal unless an operation be immediately performed. There is no time to apply to the child’s guardian. A performs the operation in spite of the entreaties of the child, intending, in good faith, the child’s benefit. A has committed no offence
9. (4) A is in a house which is on fire, with Z, a child. People below hold out a blanket. A drops the child from the house top, knowing it to be likely that the fall may kill the child, but not intending to kill the child, and intending, in good faith, the child’s benefit. Here, even if the child is killed by the fall, A has committed no offence

Explanations
Explanation.—Mere pecuniary benefit is not benefit within the meaning of sections 26, 27 and this section

Exceptions, limitations and provisos

learningObjectives: Explain the emergency / non-consensual medical doctrine under BNS s. 30.
Analyze the circumstances where consent is impossible or unavailable in time.
Examine the four statutory provisos safeguarding life.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 30 provides that nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person's consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent, or if that person is incapable of giving consent, and has no guardian or other person in lawful charge from whom it is possible to obtain consent in time for the thing to be done with benefit.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: In life-threatening emergencies where a person cannot give consent and no guardian is reachable in time, a person acting in good faith for their benefit is protected from criminal liability for necessary interventions.
statutoryFramework: Chapter III — General Exceptions, BNS s. 30 (corresponding to IPC s. 92).
Prerequisite 1: Done in good faith for the benefit of the person.
Prerequisite 2: Circumstances make it impossible to signify consent (unconsciousness, delirium), OR person incapable and no guardian reachable in time.
Proviso 1: Does NOT extend to intentional causing of death or attempt.
Proviso 2: Does NOT extend to doing what doer knows likely to cause death, unless to prevent death/grievous hurt or cure grievous disease.
Proviso 3: Does NOT extend to intentional grievous hurt or attempt, unless to prevent death/grievous hurt or cure grievous disease.
Proviso 4: Does NOT extend to abetment of any offence to which it would not extend.
essentialIngredients: Harm was caused to a person by an act done for that person's benefit.
The act was done in good faith.
The act was done without consent because the person was incapable or impossible to obtain consent from, and no guardian was available in time.
The act conformed to the four statutory provisos.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 30 is the emergency Samaritan and trauma surgeon provision. When an accident victim is brought unconscious to an emergency ward with internal hemorrhaging, waiting for consent would mean certain death. Section 30 authorizes the surgeon to operate immediately without consent. Similarly, if a house is on fire and a neighbor drops a child from the window into a rescue net, causing minor fractures, the neighbor is protected because the act was done in good faith for the child's life when parental consent was impossible in time.
examples: Teaching example (Emergency surgery): A driver is involved in a severe highway crash and arrives at hospital in a deep coma. Immediate trepanning of the skull is necessary to relieve brain pressure. The neurosurgeon operates without consent. The patient survives with partial paralysis. Section 30 protects the surgeon.

Teaching example (Rescuing child from tiger): A tiger carries off a child. A hunter fires at the tiger, knowing the bullet might strike the child, but intending in good faith to save the child's life. The bullet wounds the child slightly. The hunter is protected under s. 30 (Proviso 2 exception applies).
distinctions: Section 26 vs Section 30: Section 26 requires patient consent; Section 30 operates where consent is impossible or unavailable in time.
Section 27 vs Section 30: Section 27 requires guardian consent; Section 30 applies when the guardian cannot be contacted in time to save the person.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an emergency physician who amputated a crushed limb of an unconscious patient without family consent is criminally liable for grievous hurt.
Rule: BNS s. 30 excuses non-consensual acts done in good faith for person's benefit in emergency where consent cannot be obtained in time.

Application: Establish that the patient was comatose, immediate amputation was necessary to prevent fatal gangrene, and relatives could not be reached. The act falls under Proviso 3 (preventing death/grievous hurt).
Conclusion: Section 30 applies; no offence was committed.
